name: Ambient AI Scribes
blurb: Tools that listen to visits and draft the clinical note.
title: Ambient AI Scribes
answer: Ambient AI scribes record the conversation between clinician and patient and draft the note for review, and they are the fastest growing AI tool in care delivery. Microsoft bought Nuance, maker of DAX, for $19.7 billion, and large systems such as Kaiser Permanente have rolled scribes out across their hospitals and offices.

reading.body:
Ambient AI scribes are the fastest growing AI tool in care delivery, and the note they draft still belongs to the clinician who signs it.

The pattern is adoption through the largest buyers rather than through consumers. Microsoft paid $19.7 billion for Nuance, the maker of DAX, and Kaiser Permanente rolled scribes out across its hospitals and medical offices. Both moves put the tool inside existing clinical documentation workflows, which is where the recording, the draft, and the signature already live.

For AI scaling, the relevant constraint is not the model. It is consent to record, review of every note, and the clinician's signature. The published guidance is that patient consent is obtained and that clinicians keep reviewing and signing every note. That keeps a human in the loop on each output, and it makes the scribe a documentation tool rather than a decision tool.

The research record here is about burden and usability, not about compute or power. Five papers from 2024 through 2026 cover physician burnout, physician perspectives, a randomized trial in clinical practice, note quality, and financial productivity. None of them measures data center load, and this data does not connect scribes to the grid. What it does not cover is equally clear: no deployment counts, no error rates, and no cost figures beyond the acquisition price.
